items.informal_name: Gauss norm of a polynomial
items.type: {R : Type u_1} → {F : Type u_2} → [inst : Semiring R] → [FunLike F R ℝ] → F → ℝ → Polynomial R → ℝ
items.informal_description: The Gauss norm of a polynomial $ p $ is defined as the supremum of $ v(a_i) \cdot c^i $ over all exponents $ i $ in the support of $ p $, where $ a_i $ is the coefficient of $ X^i $ in $ p $. If $ p $ is the zero polynomial (with empty support), the Gauss norm is defined to be $ 0 $. Here, $ v $ denotes a valuation and $ c $ is a real number parameter.

items.informal_name: Mahler Measure Upper Bound by Coefficient Norms
items.type: ∀ (p : Polynomial ℂ), p.mahlerMeasure ≤ p.sum fun x a => ‖a‖
items.informal_description: For any complex polynomial $ p $, its Mahler measure satisfies $ \text{Mahler}(p) \leq \sum_{n} \|a_n\| $, where $ a_n $ are the coefficients of $ p $ and $ \|\cdot\| $ denotes the complex norm.

items.informal_name: Spectral value terms sequence
items.type: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : SeminormedRing R] → Polynomial R → ℕ → ℝ
items.informal_description: For a polynomial $ p $ over a seminormed ring $ R $, this function returns a sequence indexed by $ \mathbb{N} $ where each term is defined as $ \|p_n\|^{1/(d - n)} $ if $ n < d $, and $ 0 $ otherwise. Here, $ p_n $ denotes the coefficient of $ X^n $ in $ p $, $ d $ is the natural degree of $ p $, and $ \|\cdot\| $ is the seminorm on $ R $. This sequence captures the normed coefficients' growth rates relative to their distance from the polynomial's degree.

items.informal_name: Mahler measure of a polynomial
items.type: Polynomial ℂ → ℝ
items.informal_description: The Mahler measure of a polynomial $ p $ is defined as $ \exp(m(p)) $, where $ m(p) $ is the logarithmic Mahler measure given by $ \frac{1}{2\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} \log \|p(e^{i\theta})\| \, d\theta $, and $ \|p(e^{i\theta})\| $ denotes the complex modulus of $ p $ evaluated at $ e^{i\theta} $. If $ p $ is the zero polynomial, the Mahler measure is defined to be 0.

items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p $ over a semiring $ R $, valuation $ v $ (preserving zero and non-negative), non-negative real number $ c $, and natural number $ i $, the product $ v(a_i) \cdot c^i $ (where $ a_i $ is the coefficient of $ X^i $ in $ p $) satisfies $ v(a_i) \cdot c^i \leq \|p\|_{v,c} $, where $ \|p\|_{v,c} $ denotes the Gauss norm of $ p $ with respect to $ v $ and $ c $.

items.informal_name: Extended Distance in Product $ L^1 $ Space Equals Sum of Component Distances
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_2} {β : ι → Type u_4} [inst : Fintype ι] [inst_1 : (i : ι) → SeminormedAddCommGroup (β i)]
  (x y : PiLp 1 β), edist x y = ∑ i, edist (x.ofLp i) (y.ofLp i)
items.informal_description: For any two elements $ x $ and $ y $ in the product $ L^1 $ space $ \Pi L^1 $, the extended distance between $ x $ and $ y $ is equal to the sum of the extended distances between their corresponding components, i.e., $ \text{edist}(x, y) = \sum_{i} \text{edist}(x_i, y_i) $.

items.informal_name: Distance in Product $ L^1 $ Space Equals Component Sum
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_2} {β : ι → Type u_4} [inst : Fintype ι] [inst_1 : (i : ι) → SeminormedAddCommGroup (β i)]
  (x y : PiLp 1 β), dist x y = ∑ i, dist (x.ofLp i) (y.ofLp i)
items.informal_description: For any two elements $ x $ and $ y $ in the product $ L^1 $ space $ \Pi L^1 $, the distance between them is equal to the sum of the distances between their corresponding components, i.e., $ \mathrm{dist}(x, y) = \sum_i \mathrm{dist}(x_i, y_i) $.

items.informal_name: L^p Metric on Product Space for 0 < p < ∞
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_2} {α : ι → Type u_3} [inst : Fintype ι] [inst_1 : (i : ι) → Dist (α i)] {p : ENNReal},
  0 < p.toReal → ∀ (f g : PiLp p α), dist f g = (∑ i, dist (f.ofLp i) (g.ofLp i) ^ p.toReal) ^ (1 / p.toReal)
items.informal_description: For a finite index set $\iota$, extended non-negative real number $p$, and a family of pseudo-metric spaces $\alpha_i$, if $p$ is a positive real number ($0 < p < \infty$), then the distance between functions $f$ and $g$ in the product $L^p$ space $\Pi L^p$ is given by $\left( \sum_{i \in \iota} \text{dist}(f(i), g(i))^p \right)^{1/p}$, where $p$ is truncated to a real number.

items.informal_name: L¹ Distance in Product Space Equals Sum of Component Distances
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_2} {β : ι → Type u_4} [inst : Fintype ι] [inst_1 : (i : ι) → SeminormedAddCommGroup (β i)]
  (x y : PiLp 1 β), nndist x y = ∑ i, nndist (x.ofLp i) (y.ofLp i)
items.informal_description: In the product $ L^1 $ space over a finite index type, the non-negative distance between two elements $ x $ and $ y $ is equal to the sum of the non-negative distances between their corresponding components, i.e., $ \text{nndist}(x, y) = \sum_{i} \text{nndist}(x_i, y_i) $.

items.informal_name: Extended Distance in Product $ L^p $ Spaces Equals $ L^p $-Norm of Component Distances
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_2} {β : ι → Type u_4} [inst : Fintype ι] [inst_1 : (i : ι) → EDist (β i)] {p : ENNReal},
  0 < p.toReal → ∀ (f g : PiLp p β), edist f g = (∑ i, edist (f.ofLp i) (g.ofLp i) ^ p.toReal) ^ (1 / p.toReal)
items.informal_description: For a finite index type $\iota$ and a family of types $\beta$ equipped with extended distances, and for $p \in (0, \infty)$, the extended distance between any two functions $f, g$ in the product $L^p$ space $\Pi L^p$ is given by the $L^p$-norm of their component-wise extended distances: $$\text{edist}(f, g) = \left(\sum_{i \in \iota} \text{edist}(f(i), g(i))^p\right)^{1/p}.$$

items.informal_name: Distance of Single Elements in Product $ L^p $ Spaces Equals Component Distance
items.type:
∀ (p : ENNReal) {ι : Type u_2} (β : ι → Type u_4) [hp : Fact (1 ≤ p)] [inst : Fintype ι]
  [inst_1 : (i : ι) → SeminormedAddCommGroup (β i)] [inst_2 : DecidableEq ι] (i : ι) (b₁ b₂ : β i),
  dist (WithLp.toLp p (Pi.single i b₁)) (WithLp.toLp p (Pi.single i b₂)) = dist b₁ b₂
items.informal_description: For a finite index set $\iota$, extended real number $p \in [0, \infty]$, and a family of pseudo-metric spaces $\beta_i$, the distance between two functions in the product $L^p$ space that are non-zero only at index $i$ with values $b_1$ and $b_2$ respectively equals the distance between $b_1$ and $b_2$ in $\beta_i$. Formally, $d(\text{toLp}(\Pi.single\ i\ b_1), \text{toLp}(\Pi.single\ i\ b_2)) = d(b_1, b_2)$.

items.informal_name: Extended Distance Preservation for Single-Element Functions in Product $ L^p $ Spaces
items.type:
∀ (p : ENNReal) {ι : Type u_2} (β : ι → Type u_4) [hp : Fact (1 ≤ p)] [inst : Fintype ι]
  [inst_1 : (i : ι) → SeminormedAddCommGroup (β i)] [inst_2 : DecidableEq ι] (i : ι) (b₁ b₂ : β i),
  edist (WithLp.toLp p (Pi.single i b₁)) (WithLp.toLp p (Pi.single i b₂)) = edist b₁ b₂
items.informal_description: For any index $ i $ and elements $ b_1, b_2 $ in the $ i $-th component space, the extended distance between the $ L^p $-embeddings of the single-element functions $ \Pi.single(i, b_1) $ and $ \Pi.single(i, b_2) $ in the product $ L^p $ space equals the extended distance between $ b_1 $ and $ b_2 $ in their original space, i.e., $ \text{edist}(\text{toLp}(p, \Pi.single(i, b_1)), \text{toLp}(p, \Pi.single(i, b_2))) = \text{edist}(b_1, b_2) $.
